BuildingPerk_Automaton_Description: A rainpunk automaton will permanently occupy one workplace. It doesn't eat, and it doesn't need rest. Its sole purpose is to work. Automatons have no chance of producing double yields.

BuildingPerk_BlightPost_BlightFighterSpe: A more compact version of the famous Blight Fighter flamethrower. Blight Fighters assigned to this Blight Post move {0} faster.
BuildingPerk_BlightPost_CystBurnSpeed_De: An innovative improvement to the flamethrower ignition system. Blight Fighters and Blight Automatons at this Blight Post need {0} seconds less to burn a Blightrot Cyst.
BuildingPerk_BlightPost_CystGenerationRa: Blight Fighters regularly inspect production buildings. For each Blight Fighter assigned to a building with this upgrade, Blightrot Cysts will appear {0} slower when using Rain Engines (up to a maximum of 90%).
BuildingPerk_BlightPost_PurgingFireProdS: Only the most experienced Blight Fighters can operate this machine. Workers at this Blight Post have a {0} higher chance of producing twice the amount of <sprite name="blight fuel"> Purging Fire.

ConditionalNeedEffect_1BuildingDestroyed: The storm in this region is extremely violent. Once this effect is activated, you'll have to pay {1} {0} (multiplied by the number of years). If you don't, 3 buildings in your settlement will become ruins.
ConditionalNeedEffect_3BuildingsDestroye: A terrifying sound from a raging sky. Every {0} seconds, {1} buildings are destroyed by lightning.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Aurora_Desc: The weather in these lands sometimes enables you to peer beyond the veil of clouds.
ConditionalNeedEffect_BitterRain_Desc: A cold, half-frozen sleet is falling from the sky.
ConditionalNeedEffect_BlightrotAfterDeat: This damp and rotting landscape is the perfect breeding ground for sickness. Every villager that dies during the storm instantly turns into a Blood Flower.
ConditionalNeedEffect_BuildingMaterialsP: The rain dissolves some of the resources transported to your Warehouse. Recipes producing building materials yield {0} fewer goods.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Cloudburst_Desc: Even the hardiest villagers need some sort of cover in this weather.
ConditionalNeedEffect_ColdFront_Desc: The wind is bone-chillingly cold, making every exposed bit of skin sting painfully after just a few moments.
ConditionalNeedEffect_ColdSnap_Desc: A sudden drop of temperature can cause extreme hunger.
ConditionalNeedEffect_DeadlyLights_Desc: Those lured by the lights may not come back. It's better to keep people focused and occupied.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Downpour_Desc: The heavy rain and cold climate are extremely taxing on the villagers. Without proper shelter and nourishment, the people will have to compensate somehow.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Eclipse_Desc: The sun is obscured even more than usual. Almost as if it's gone missing for a while.
ConditionalNeedEffect_EerieSong_Desc: There are no words, or even a melody. Those who go looking for the song don't usually return...
ConditionalNeedEffect_EuphoricVapours_De: There is something in the air that invokes pleasant moods. The effect is especially strong when the body is well nourished.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Fog_Desc: A veil of moisture obscures vision. It is hard to walk in these conditions.
ConditionalNeedEffect_FoorProdSpeedSlowe: The rain smells like Blightrot... Global food production is slowed by {0} per Hostility level (counting from level 0).
ConditionalNeedEffect_FreshBreeze_Desc: A refreshing gust of air lifts the spirit. Those with their basic needs taken care of are more willing to work.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Generic_Status: To PREVENT it, fulfill the following need(s): {0}
ConditionalNeedEffect_Generic_Status_Pos: To GAIN it, fulfill the following need(s): {0}
ConditionalNeedEffect_GoodsForTrade_Desc: The Queen's generosity knows no limits. Gain {1} every time you sell goods worth {0} Amber.
ConditionalNeedEffect_GrowingFoodConsump: Working in this environment requires a lot of energy. Villagers have a higher chance of consuming twice the amount of food on each break ({0} for each Hostility level, counting from level 0).
ConditionalNeedEffect_GrowingServiceCons: Some goods seem to be mysteriously disappearing. Maybe there's a thief in the settlement? Villagers have a higher chance of consuming twice the amount of goods when using services ({0} for each Hostility level, counting from level 0).
ConditionalNeedEffect_Hailstorm_Desc: Death by a thousand hailstones. There is no way to be safe without a roof over your head.
ConditionalNeedEffect_InkInCollector_Des: The rain in this region has a weird red hue and iron taste to it. <sprite name="[crafting] pigment"> Pigment ({0}) can be collected in the Rain Collector in drizzle season.
ConditionalNeedEffect_InsectsInScavenger: Insects are extremely easy to collect after heavy rainfall. During drizzle season, workers in the Scavengers' Camp can gather <sprite name="[food raw] insects"> insects ({0}) from insect nodes.
ConditionalNeedEffect_InvigoratingWinds_: The smell of fresh air. Energizing for those not distracted by its coldness.
ConditionalNeedEffect_LessMetalProduced_: Acid rain is slowly eating away at all metal objects. Producing Copper Bars, Crystalized Dew, and all goods that use metal ingots yields {0} fewer goods.
ConditionalNeedEffect_Melancholy_Desc: A humdrum and peaceful atmosphere brings back memories of the Citadel: home cooked meals and cozy beds.
ConditionalNeedEffect_MoreDepositCharges: Small, energizing drops cause uncontrollable growth in certain species. All gathering nodes discovered during drizzle season have more charges: +{0} to small ones, and +{1} to large ones.
ConditionalNeedEffect_NauseousSpores_Des: A sickening smell is in the air. Villagers need something to help them focus.
ConditionalNeedEffect_NoImpatienceReduct: Harsh weather conditions make it impossible to reach the Citadel. Gaining Reputation doesn't lower Impatience.
ConditionalNeedEffect_PiercingWinds_Desc: Extremely strong winds make it difficult to sustain the Holy Flame. Fuel consumption in Hearths is increased by {0}.
ConditionalNeedEffect_RegularStorm_Desc: Homeless villagers are especially vulnerable during the storm.
ConditionalNeedEffect_RepFromResolveBloc: No amount of amenities can distract villagers from the terrifying storm. Reputation generated from Resolve grows {0} slower.
ConditionalNeedEffect_ResinForWood_Desc: A red, sticky substance is oozing out from beneath the tree bark. Gain {0} every time woodcutters cut down a tree.
ConditionalNeedEffect_SlowGathering_Desc: The ground is moving and swaying from all the rainwater it’s absorbed. Gathering speed is decreased by {0}.
ConditionalNeedEffect_SlowWoodCutting_De: The trees seem to come to life during the storm... Woodcutting is {0} slower, but each fallen tree gives {1}.
ConditionalNeedEffect_SpeedGathering_Des: The forest's fruits are so ripe, they almost fall into the basket on their own. Gathering speed is increased by {0}.
ConditionalNeedEffect_StrangeLights_Desc: People are reporting seeing strange visages in the woods. They need something to put their minds at ease.
ConditionalNeedEffect_StrangeVisions_Des: They offer inspiration for open minds...
ConditionalNeedEffect_SunFestivities_Des: Having ways to celebrate and express themselves keeps people more eager to work for the common good.
ConditionalNeedEffect_SwarmsBad_Desc: Constant bites and cuts don't really hurt that much, but are certainly annoying for those without proper protection.
ConditionalNeedEffect_ToxicRain_Desc: Everything grows and blooms under this heavy rainfall, even if it shouldn't.
ConditionalNeedEffect_UnderTheOpenSky_De: Lack of shelter during such a malevolent storm is simply gross neglect of villagers.
ConditionalNeedEffect_WoodcutterCapacity: The evaporating rainwater has made the wood a lot lighter in this region. Woodcutters can carry {1} more goods in drizzle season.
ConditionalNeedEffect_WoodPaymentForVill: Only the Sacred Flame can protect the settlement from the darkness surrounding it. Pay {1} {0} for every villager in your settlement. If you don't pay for all of them, 2 people will leave.
If you don't deliver the required goods for the sacrifice, {0} villagers will disappear.
Content_Tip_CameraRotation: Use the middle mouse button to rotate the camera.
Content_Tip_Cycle: The Cycle is a vicious force of nature that ravages the land every few years. The time left before the next Blightstorm is indicated on the bottom of the screen in the World Map view.
Content_Tip_DangerousGlades: Dangerous glades are always marked. They are rich in resources and rewards, but be sure you're prepared to deal with the threats they contain.
Content_Tip_Destruction: Destroying a building will refund all the resources that were spent on its construction.
Content_Tip_MovingBuildings: You can move some buildings by selecting the 'Move' button in the building window.
Content_Tip_Expansion: You can build Small Hearths and Warehouses to expand your settlement - villagers will always rest at the nearest Hearth, and take their goods to the nearest Warehouse.
Content_Tip_Factions: Different factions are constantly trying to settle on the World Map. If they succeed, they will drain Citadel Resources from nearby areas.
Content_Tip_Fuel: Wood isn't the only thing that can be burned in the hearth. There are also other, more efficient types of fuel like oil and coal.
Content_Tip_Lore1: The never-ending rain carries a magical charge with it. It's dangerous, but very useful at the same time, and can be used to create powerful Rainpunk technology.
Content_Tip_Lore2: The Smoldering City is the only safe haven in the known world. It was built on ancient ruins, left behind by the long-dead Great Civilization.
Content_Tip_Lore3: The Marshlands are considered by scholars to be one giant underground fungus. Some even claim that it is sentient.
Content_Tip_Lore4: Clearance is the warmest season. The rain is light, and there's even a bit of sunshine during the day. It's the ideal time for harvesting crops.
Content_Tip_Lore5: The storm is a time of destruction and chaos. Strong winds and relentless rainfall make it difficult to work outside.
Content_Tip_Lore6: Drizzle is the calmest season - a time of growth and regeneration. The rain is heavy, but its negative effects are milder than during the rest of the year.
Content_Tip_Modifiers: Some areas of the world have special modifiers. These objects make it harder to win, but also give better rewards.
Content_Tip_Moodlets: Every map has its own Forest Mysteries - special seasonal effects that will influence your settlements. Beneficial Forest Mysteries trigger during drizzle season, while dangerous ones are active during the storm.
Content_Tip_NeedCycle: Are your villagers hungry even though you have food in your Warehouse? Just wait for them to rest at the Hearth. Then they’ll have chance to satisfy their needs.
Content_Tip_NewContent: You unlock new buildings, cornerstones, and traders by leveling up. The higher the difficulty of a game, the more experience points you’ll earn.
Content_Tip_Recipes: Most recipes have variable ingredients. This allows you to switch between different input goods, yet achieve the same result.
Content_Tip_ReputationPoints: Reputation Points can be acquired by completing orders, finishing Glade Events, and keeping your villagers' Resolve very high.
Content_Tip_Resting: Villagers need breaks. They will regularly return to the Hearth to rest and fulfill their needs.
Content_Tip_Storage: Each resource in a building has its own storage limit. When a resource reaches its limit, it will be moved to a warehouse.
Content_Tip_TraderAssault: Don't have enough Amber for a trade? You can always assault a trader and rob them. But beware, this has dire consequences!
Content_Tip_Upgrades: You can spend the Citadel Resources you’ve acquired to buy upgrades in the Smoldering City.
Content_Tutorial3_LockedReason: To unlock the Rainpunk & Blightrot tutorial scenario, you must first buy the Obsidian Archive Level 6 upgrade in the Smoldering City.
